bull.argument: Costco's 2026 filing shows a business compounding on several fronts. Net sales rose 10% to $297,247 million, and comparable sales grew 8%, with 7% growth excluding currency and gasoline effects, so the core engine is not just being flattered by fuel prices. Net income increased 14% to $9,226 million, and diluted EPS rose to $20.76 from $18.21. Membership fee revenue grew 11% to $5,907 million, and the renewal rate stood at 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada, a recurring, high-visibility income stream. Digitally-enabled comparable sales jumped 21%, showing the e-commerce push is working. Management also raised the quarterly dividend 13%, signaling confidence in cash generation. The filing does flag real risks, including heavy concentration in U.S. and Canadian operations and California, and cyber and AI exposure. But the reported numbers show growth in members, sales and profits together, which is the profile a long-term holder wants.

claims.claim: Core comparable sales growth was strong even after stripping out currency and gasoline effects.
claims.quote: Increases in comparable sales excluding the impact of changes in foreign-currency and gasoline prices (1) : U.S. 7 % 7 % 5 %

claims.claim: Membership fee revenue grew 11%, supported by high renewal rates.
claims.quote: At the end of 2026, member renewal rates were 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide.

claims.claim: Net income rose 14% and the board raised the quarterly dividend 13%.
claims.quote: Net income increased 14% to $9,226, $20.76 per diluted share, compared to $8,099, $18.21 per diluted share in 2025

bear.argument: The filing shows a business whose results lean heavily on factors management does not control. U.S. and Canadian operations generated 86% and 83% of net sales and operating income, and California alone is 26% of U.S. net sales, so a slowdown in one concentrated market would hit results hard. Growth also leaned on gasoline: higher gasoline prices added $3,501 million, or 130 basis points, to net sales, and the filing notes that rising gasoline prices reduce gross margin percentage. Excluding gasoline inflation, gross margin rose 10 basis points only in the sense management describes, and core merchandise margins fell 11 basis points. Net income was helped by a $184 million IEEPA tariff refund, of which a portion was reinvested in member prices, so that one-time benefit is not clearly repeatable. Finally, the filing warns of rising AI-driven cyber threats and of 'no guarantee' that controls will be sufficient, a risk that could affect member confidence in a business the filing calls critically dependent on it.

claims.claim: Results are concentrated in U.S. and Canadian operations and in California.
claims.quote: Our financial and operational performance is highly dependent on our U.S. and Canadian operations, which comprised 86% and 83% of net sales and operating income in 2026.

claims.claim: Gasoline prices materially boosted reported net sales growth.
claims.quote: Higher gasoline prices positively impacted net sales by $3,501, or 130 basis points, with a 12% increase in the average price per gallon.

claims.claim: Core merchandise margins weakened, and the net income gain included a one-time tariff refund.
claims.quote: offset by an 11 basis point decrease in core merchandise categories

bull.argument: The bear case is right that concentration and risk are real. U.S. and Canadian operations produced 86% and 83% of net sales and operating income, and California is a large share of U.S. sales. But the filing's own data shows the core engine is not just fuel. Comparable sales excluding currency and gasoline rose 7% in the U.S. and 7% in total, and digitally-enabled comparable sales rose 21%. Stripping out gasoline inflation, gross margin percentage rose 10 basis points to 11.22%. The tariff refund was $184, about 2% of the $9,226 million net income, and management says it intends to reinvest the majority of the refunds for members, so it is not the source of the profit growth. Membership fee revenue grew 11%, and U.S. and Canada renewal rates held at 92.3%. The cyber and AI warnings are disclosed risks, not reported incidents, and the filing notes a 13% dividend increase. Growth in sales, members, and earnings, with a rising dividend, is a strong profile despite the concentration risks.

claims.claim: Comparable sales growth held up after excluding currency and gasoline effects.
claims.quote: Increases in comparable sales excluding the impact of changes in foreign-currency and gasoline prices (1) : U.S. 7 % 7 % 5 %

claims.claim: Gross margin percentage rose once gasoline price inflation was excluded.
claims.quote: Excluding the impact of gasoline price inflation on net sales, gross margin percentage was 11.22%, an increase of 10 basis points.

claims.claim: Management intends to reinvest most tariff refunds in member value rather than keep them as profit.
claims.quote: we intend to continue to invest the majority of the refunds in increased value for the member

bear.argument: The opponent's numbers are accurate but incomplete. Ex-gasoline comparable sales growth of 7% is strong, yet the reported 8% total and 10% net sales growth were lifted by a 12% rise in gasoline prices, which added $3,501 million, or 130 basis points, to net sales. The 11.22% ex-gasoline margin is management's adjusted figure; reported gross margin fell three basis points to 11.09%, and core merchandise margins dropped 11 basis points. On the tariff refund, the $184 million is small against net income, but the bigger point is that reported profit growth of 14% rests partly on a benefit that will not repeat, and the filing says 'refunds may be delayed,' so the timing is uncertain. Membership growth is also softer than it looks: fee income increases from the 2024 price hike accounted for about 30% of membership income growth in 2026. Finally, the filing says it is 'highly dependent' on California and that AI-driven cyber threats could erode 'member confidence,' which it calls critical to the model. A high-multiple long-term holder is paying for uninterrupted execution in a concentrated, low-margin business that the filing itself says is exposed to these risks.

claims.claim: Reported gross margin percentage declined, and core merchandise margins fell.
claims.quote: Gross margin percentage decreased three basis points.

claims.claim: Membership income growth was partly driven by a one-time fee increase.
claims.quote: The fee income increase accounted for approximately 30% and 40% of membership income growth during 2026 and 2025.

claims.claim: Tariff refunds are uncertain in timing and were partly passed to members.
claims.quote: For a small percentage of transactions where corrections are required, refunds may be delayed as the government continues to implement the IEEPA refund process.

judge.reasoning: Both sides cite verified quotes from the filing and engage the other's main points: the bull concedes concentration risk and reframes the tariff refund as small, while the bear concedes ex-gasoline comparable growth and disputes only the adjusted margin framing. The bull's quoted 10bp ex-gasoline margin increase and the bear's reported 3bp decline are both accurate descriptions of different measures, so neither side fully wins the margin argument. Overall the debate is evenly matched, with each side landing strong points and neither clearly outweighing the other.
